headline: A 2020 resolution would have required the President to end U.S. military hostilities against Iran unless Congress declared war or specifically authorized them, but Congress did not override the veto.
what_it_does: If adopted, this joint resolution would have directed the President to stop using U.S. Armed Forces in hostilities against Iran. The only exceptions would have been a congressional declaration of war or a specific authorization for the use of military force against Iran. The President vetoed the measure, and the Senate failed to override that veto on May 7, 2020.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. military service members deployed in the Middle East
who_it_affects.how: They would have been pulled out of combat operations against Iran unless Congress approved those operations.
They would have kept the constitutional power to decide whether the country goes to war with Iran.
